In a recent development, even though I finally embraced wearing leggings last year, I still hesitate when it comes to winterizing my running gear—even when the “feels like” temp is 28 degrees Fahrenheit on a 34-degree day. The simplest gear that transforms my getup, doesn’t make me regret overdressing, and helps me stay warm when the weather begins taking its nippy turn? Gloves. My pair of choice is the Smartwool Active Fleece Insulated.

According to recent reports, of all the runs and races I’ve underdressed for, the one accessory I always regret not putting on is a pair of gloves. I’m the kind of person whose hands are constantly cold. (Healthcare friends, I’m sorry for having fingers that refuse to get a quick oxygen read.).

I could go the mitts route, and I do when I need an extra layer over my gloved fingers (yes, I double up). But the thing about running, especially when you’re training for Boston in the spring, is that you need to be able to spread your 10 digits and use them to retrieve fuel—or lip balm or a Kleenex—from the depths of your pockets, which requires more dexterity than mittens allow.

Industry observers note that I like Smartwool’s gloves because of their range of sizes, though I will admit the extra small is still slightly long in the tips due to their unisex sizing. The gloves are double-layer knit and have a blend of merino wool and polyester to thermoregulate your hands and wick away sweat. The overlay panels serve as windproof protection.

Besides warmth and the usage of my fingers, the Active Fleece also provides visibility, thanks to a reflective logo and piping on the back of the hand. Being seen is notable when daylight hours are shorter and I need to log that run before dawn or can only fit in a workout at dusk.

The index and thumb have touchscreen-compatible pads. I wouldn’t recommend them for long-winded texts since, through my own experience, messages aren’t always accurate. But it’s nice that I can type into Google Maps or use dictation and send, “PICK ME UP—I MADE A HORRIBLE MISTAKE” with a location pin.

According to recent reports, sometimes the best test is when you’re not running. On our first chilly morning this fall, I got up early on a Sunday and waited to cheer at mile 10 of a half marathon. The precursor to the waiting was pacing every block in a half-mile radius, trying to figure out if I was actually on the race course.

In a recent development, when the runners came in and I finally found the right sidewalk corner, the stutter in my voice told me I should have worn two extra layers. Despite my frozen core, I was surprised I still had the feeling in my Smartwool gloved hands.

Sources indicate that the best part of that morning besides being able to type out post-cheer coffee shop directions? Sticking it out so I could encourage runners with more cowbell.

Shop Smartwool Active Fleece Insulated Gloves at smartwool.com.

Black Friday is here, and it’s a great time to save on Garmin devices. Electronics always make great holiday gifts for cyclists. Whether you’re buying for a rider in your life or upgrading your cycling computer, radar, smart trainer, or power meter on a budget, the holiday season is the best time to score big savings. And Garmin makes some of the best and most popular training and navigation devices for road, gravel, fitness, and mountain bike riders.

According to recent reports, garmin’s GPS computers, smartwatches, radar taillights, power pedals, and Tacx indoor trainers have received great reviews from Bicycling editors and top rankings in our head-to-head tests. The brand’s gear doesn’t often go on deep sale, so these early drops are worth jumping on before they sell out. However, with so many models marked down across both categories, it’s easy to feel overwhelmed. Plus, devices can look similar at first glance, but the details matter when choosing the right tool for riding, training, and everyday fitness.

Garmin GPS head units are one of the smartest upgrades you can make to your road, gravel, mountain, or electric bike, and a much safer alternative than strapping your phone to the bars to see your route. Cycling computers also capture, process, and display data from accessories like heart rate monitors, power meters, and even electronic shifting to help you ride better, train smarter, and stay connected. And because Garmin lets you customize nearly everything—from data fields to navigation screens—you can tailor exactly what highlights up.

Buying Tip: Buying previous-generation cycling computers is a great way to save money. Older models usually have almost the same performance at a major discount. Cyclists often even prefer the old models if they’re lighterweight or have better battery life.

Cycling radar is one of the most important pieces of bicycle technology released in the last decade. On-bike radar systems mount to the rear of your bike and feature an integrated taillight. Paired with a cycling computer or smartwatch, they notify you about vehicles approaching from behind so you can move out of the way. They are a must-have item for road and gravel riders.

Not sure which radar you need? Check out my comparison below.

In a recent development, buying Tip: Garmin is a pioneer in cycling radar tech and makes the most reliable, consistent systems. The Varia RTL515 is our benchmark and best-value pick, while the RearVue 820 is newer and more powerful; it’s our choice for best performance. The RCT715 is the 515 with an integrated rear-facing camera.

Sources indicate that while dedicated cycling computers are the go-to choice for road, gravel, and data-heavy training, many riders prefer Garmin’s smartwatches because they keep everything in one place, especially when they track more than bike rides—anyone who mixes riding with running, hiking, paddling, strength training, or even walking the dog. Garmin watches have powerful GPS, workout metrics, and daily health data in a streamlined device that’s always with you (and they even tell time).

Industry observers note that buying Tip: Mountain bikers often appreciate the simplicity and safety of recording their rides from the wrist rather than risking a pricey head unit in a crash. Triathletes, duathletes, and cyclocross racers love the seamless transitions a watch allows. There’s no need to swap devices or merge files after an event.

Recent findings suggest that most riders know Garmin from its computers, smartwatches, and cycling radar. But Garmin also owns the indoor trainer brand Tacx. Its smart trainers and indoor bikes are highly regarded for their excellent performance, integration, and useful features. One cool feature we love—especially if you live somewhere prone to winter power outages—is that the Neo 2T generates its own resistance electromagnetically. That means you don’t have to scrap your workout prepares just because the lights go out.

Buying Tip: Smart trainers are great for riding in virtual worlds like Zwift. For a deep dive into more great indoor trainers and buying info, check out my story “Ready to Ride Indoors? Here’s How to Pick the Best Trainer.”.

According to recent reports, want to step up your training for next season? The best way to measure cycling gains is by training with power—and for that, you need a power meter. Power pedals, like Garmin’s Rally series, are easier to install than crank-based power meter options. Plus, you can swap power pedals easily between bikes. This not only saves cost, but it also gives you consistent data from bike to bike.

Buying Tip: Garmin offers a handy option to buy its power meter in a package including two pedal styles (road and mountain bike/gravel) with swappable spindles. This way you can measure power across riding disciplines.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that personally, I cannot fathom running without some form of entertainment. And I get that finding the best headphones for running is crucial to getting through those miles, no matter if you’re a casual jogger or hardcore marathoner. But with a dizzying array of options out there—from earbuds to bone-conduction headphones to sporty sunglasses—it’s hard to pick which ones you want or need. We have even come around to over-the-ear headphones for running that are so popular with Gen Z. And we found a really comfy pair that’s sweat resistant, and the sound? Chef’s kiss.

We did the hard work for you, testing a gazillion different headphones, paying the same close attention to these that we do to shoes to bring you only the cream of the crop. You can forget about constantly readjusting loose earbuds or battling tangled wires, because these selections were chosen to stay put and deliver crystal-clear sound mile after mile, so that when you get to the good part of your podcast, it’s not going to drop out. We’re talking about headphones that can handle sweat, rain, snow, and the accidental drop, so you can focus on your stride, not your tech.

Become a Runner’s World+ member for exclusive access to product testing opportunities!

The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 headphones are a real game changer for runners who want great sound without sacrificing safety or comfort. Aly Ellis, our director of content hype, sums it up perfectly: “These are my favorite running headphones ever, specifically, the Kipchoge edition. They get loud enough that you can hear them while running, but you can hear noise and traffic around you. I listen to music, podcasts, and audiobooks while wearing mine, and they all sound great!”.

That open-ear design is the magic here—it keeps you aware of your surroundings, whether you’re dodging bikes on a trail or crossing busy streets.

Sound quality is where the OpenRun Pro 2 really shines, thanks to dual drivers that blend crisp highs from bone conduction with deep bass from air conduction tech, delivering a unique, immersive sound. You get 12 hours of battery life, so you can go for long runs (or even a marathon) without worrying about charging. The fit is secure and stable, with ergonomic ear hooks and a memory wire frame that stays put no matter how much you sweat or move around.

Industry observers note that another standout is the dedicated EQ modes in the Shokz app, letting you tweak your audio for different environments—boost it when it’s noisy, or keep it classic for everyday runs. Calls are crystal clear, even in windy conditions, thanks to dual microphones and smart noise reduction. If you want headphones that sound great, stay comfortable, and keep you safe and aware, the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 is tough to beat.

The JLab Go Sport+ headphones are a fantastic option for runners and fitness fans who want reliable, sweatproof wireless earbuds without breaking the bank. These earbuds are all about getting the basics right: with an IP55 sweat- and dirt-resistance rating, they can handle even your sweatiest, muddiest workouts. The over-ear hooks and three sizes of silicone ear tips mean you get a secure, comfortable fit—no matter how much you move, these buds stay put without pinching or slipping.

One of the biggest highlights is battery life: You get 9-plus hours per earbud, plus another 26-plus from the charging case, for a whopping 35 hours total. That’s more than enough for a week of workouts, and the integrated USB cable makes recharging the case a breeze. Pairing is simple, especially if you’re on Android thanks to Google Fast Pair, and the connection is rock-solid up to 50 feet away.

Industry observers note that the sound quality could be better. It can sound a bit tinny and awkward when you’re expecting something bolder or more rounded. For under $30, though, they’re nothing to laugh at. And with the features and battery life, we think it’s a fair trade.

The JLab Go Sport+ also includes a "Be Aware" mode, which lets in ambient sound so you can stay alert on busy streets or trails. And with the JLab app, you can customize your sound profile and touch controls to suit your preferences. While the audio quality isn’t as rich or dynamic as that of some pricier competitors—think a bit hollow, especially if you’re an audiophile—it’s more than good enough for podcasts, playlists, and calls on the go.

All in all, if you’re after affordable, dependable, and comfortable wireless earbuds for running or the gym, the JLab Go Sport+ is a solid pick that punches above its price point.

Recent findings suggest that the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 earbuds are designed to stay put, thanks to flexible earhooks and five ear tip sizes, so you can focus on your run instead of fiddling with your headphones. The IPX4 water resistance means they’ll handle sweat and rain without a hitch.

In a recent development, the sound quality is on point—expect punchy bass and crisp highs (as someone who has worn these, Hamilton has never sounded better), which blend into a nicely balanced sound that makes your playlists pop. Its active noise cancellation and transparency modes are handy, letting you block out the gym clatter and your children’s video game sounds when you want to focus, or let in the world when you’re running on the street and would rather not be taken out by a minivan.

Battery life is another substantial win. You get up to 10 hours per bud (8 if you’re using ANC), and the charging case stretches your total playtime to an astonishing 45 hours. Forgot to charge? No worries—a quick five-minute boost gives you over an hour of listening time.

In a recent development, there are a few drawbacks: the price is on the higher side, and the upcoming heart rate monitoring feature isn’t quite polished yet, especially for iPhone people. Plus, there’s no customizable EQ, which might disappoint anyone who likes to fine-tune their sound.

Overall, the Powerbeats Pro 2 are a nice pick if you want secure, great-sounding earbuds that go the distance—just don’t expect them to replace your fitness tracker.

This is the second generation of the Bose Ultra Open earbuds, and I am a huge fan. Both Dengate and I had thousands of miles on the first generation, and this set of buds is proving to hold its own. The improvements are minor, but notable. They include deeper bass, higher volume, more controls, a slightly improved fit, and a better IP rating.

In a recent development, here’s the thing: most open-ear headphones are something to be desired when it comes to bass and high tones. They can lack richness and that “oomph” you look for when you’re listening to your music. The first generation of the Bose Ultra Open was leaps and bounds above most open-ear, but the bass was still a bit stingy. This set, however, gives you so much more boom for your buck. And you can feel it—seriously—not only is it pumping the sound into your ear, but the vibration is felt in the shell of your ear, which does take some getting used to.

The fit is my second favorite bit of these earbuds. They wrap around the shell of your ear without squeezing or pinching, and they sit gently upon the lower curve above your earlobe. I can and do wear these all day long, taking calls, listening to music, and generally going about my day. The battery life could be better, but for all that sound and comfort, I’m not mad.

The biggest issue with over-the-ear headphones is that sweat can short them out. It’s not all of them; gaming headphones or gaming/multipurpose headphones by and large are designed with sweaty gaming sessions in mind, so they don’t typically short out as often. Casual headphones, on the other hand, have suffered from sweat shock. Not these. These were made with workouts in mind, and they keep all the comfort, all the “leave me alone” energy, and all that great sound. They’re also sweat-resistant and ever so slightly more breathable than your standard over-the-ear cans.

According to recent reports, these are incredibly comfortable, stay put, and the music? It just sounds so glorious. I ran a 20-miler in these, listening to a bunch of film scores, and the music from Interstellar transported me to a place where I didn’t hate myself quite so much. They do, of course, make your ears a bit warm after you’ve been wearing them a while, but honestly? I was running at elevation (over 8,000 feet) and I actually loved both the warmth and the wind protection they provided me. And they sounded just as good at two and a half hours as they did at minute one of charge.

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 are the gold standard for wireless earbuds, and also the most ubiquitous. They’re the overwhelming favorite earbuds on the market. I think that’s largely because the moment you pop them in, you notice the comfortable, secure fit (thanks to four ear tip sizes) and Apple’s signature ergonomic design. Whether you’re commuting, running, or just trying to listen to your romance novel audiobook without scandalizing your family, these buds stay put and feel featherlight.

Thanks to a custom high-excursion driver and Apple's H2 chip, your hype music comes in sharp and booming, even in loud environments. Apple's active noise cancellation is among the best of the best, and adaptive transparency mode lets you hear what’s going on around you at a level you can stand when you’re trying to get your workout on. Adaptive audio and conversation awareness are new in this version and automatically blend ANC and transparency, or lower your volume when you start talking. Personally, I didn’t notice this sound degradation, but my husband claims it’s noticeable to him.

Battery life is pretty good—up to 10 hours per bud and 24 hours total with the little white case. The case itself is instantly recognizable, supports wireless and USB-C charging, and even has a speaker and Find My integration for those inevitable “where did I put them?” moments. (And not for anything, there’s about a million ways to customize these if you’re on Etsy.) They’re also IPX4 rated, so they’ll handle sweat and a little rain, though they’re not meant for swimming laps like the Suunto Aqua.

The live translate feature is cool, but testing it with my Mandarin-speaking husband revealed lags and a few glitches. (And, well, some things translated very oddly, and not in a good way.) The heart rate function is similar. It's better than my watch, but not as good as a chest strap, and I think that's pretty fair, honestly.

They aren’t perfect, though. The case scratches easily, and you get the best experience only with Apple devices. Still, for iPhone owners who want top-tier sound, seamless controls, and noise cancellation that actually works, the AirPods Pro 3 will be an obvious go-to for many runners.

Industry observers note that the Sony Sport Earbuds are cute and unbelievably comfy, especially in the eye-catching pink colorway that adds a fun pop to your gear. The marbled case is a stylish bonus in my opinion (yes, it's twee; no, I don't care). These earbuds stayed perfectly put and cozy during a four-hour, 30-mile run—no slipping, no discomfort.The noise-canceling tech blocks out distractions so you can fully dive into your music, though they’re not the best for driving since they quiet things down too much, even in transparency mode. Touch controls feel smooth, with volume adjusting in tiny, gentle steps—no sudden bursts to startle your ears. Sound quality is crisp and lively thanks to dynamic drivers, and Bluetooth 5.3 keeps the connection rock solid. Battery life is marathon-ready, lasting up to 8 hours with noise canceling on. These buds combine cuteness, comfort, and serious performance for anyone on the move.

I’m never going to do a triathlon, because bicycles are terrifying, but swimming? Sweating? Those I do. And listen, because of my disgustingly sweaty head and love of the water, I’ve dunked a lot of headphones in the name of journalism, and most of them did not survive the experience. The H2O Audio Tri 2 Pro ($199) took every chlorine-ridden and sweat-soaked hour.

According to recent reports, the headphones' IPX8 rating is 12 feet, making submersion time effectively unlimited, which means they outlast me in the pool or the ocean (yes, I love open-water swimming by a considerable margin). The bone conduction design pairs with earplugs for genuinely decent underwater audio. It has real bass response, not the sad tinny thumping you’d expect. As someone who prefers to run to a mix of T. Swift and My Chemical Romance, I like it to sound as emotional as possible to keep me motivated.

Sources indicate that but the Playlist+ feature is what sets this set of cans apart from others: you can download eight gigabytes of music directly to your headphones, so you can leave your phone in the pool locker or locked in your car—your playlist is ready to go the second you jump in. No phone, no Bluetooth dropouts, no excuses. On land, the sound is firmly good enough, and yes, the buttons need a firmware lesson in responsiveness. But for swimmers and sweaty eddies? This thing is a boss.

Industry observers note that shokz leveled up with this pair of headphones. For years, they’ve been known primarily for their stellar bone-conduction headphones, but with these noise-canceling, open-ear hooks, they’re shifting the narrative for their brand. Černá tried these as well. “I was pretty skeptical at first—no way these earbuds could withstand all the bouncing while I run and not move,” she said. “Surprise: they don’t bounce around! It’s almost as if they’re magnetically attached to my ear.".

Industry observers note that thanks to the dual noise-canceling microphones embedded in the headphones, they were audible in a variety of conditions, including some heavy wind. A feature Černá loves is the smart wear function, which turns the phones off when you’re not wearing them, keeping your place in your audiobook or podcast. And for the ADHD-addled, like myself? Being able to ping your earbuds is honestly so clutch. Forget where they are? Don’t worry, you can find them.

They’re comfy, they can handle a decent amount of sweat and precipitation, they’re feature-rich, and honestly, just a great experience overall.

Choosing the right running headphones can really make your run. With so many options available, it’s key to consider which features are most important for your needs. To help guide your decision, here are some key factors to consider when selecting the perfect running headphones.

Sources indicate that in-ear headphones, also known as earbuds, fit directly into the ear canal. They are often compact and lightweight, making them highly portable. In-ear headphones can offer good sound isolation, blocking out some external noise and, depending on the fit, a decent level of bass. They often come with various ear tip sizes to make sure they’re not going to fall out of your ears.

Recent findings suggest that hook headphones typically feature a design with hooks that wrap around the ears for added stability. This makes them popular for activities like running or exercising, where a secure fit is crucial to prevent them from falling out. Hook headphones can come in various styles, including earbuds with hooks and over-ear, open-ear styles with hooks.

Bone conduction headphones work by transmitting sound vibrations through the bones of your skull, bypassing the eardrums. This allows you to listen to audio while keeping your ears open to your surroundings. This is especially useful for runners who need to be aware of traffic or other environmental sounds.

Open-ear headphones are designed to sit outside the ear, allowing you to hear both your audio and the environment around you. They don't block your ear canal, so you remain aware of your surroundings, which is helpful for safety during outdoor activities. However, they may leak sound, and the audio quality might not be as immersive as other types.

Recent findings suggest that headphones with storage typically include onboard memory for storing music files directly on the headphones. This eliminates the need to carry a separate device for music playback. This feature is particularly convenient for runners or swimmers who prefer not to bring their phones along.

While our testers experienced no immediate problems with water or sweat damage, prolonged exposure to moisture and salt can harm earbuds not designed to repel these elements. That’s why we found it imperative that we checked out each device’s “IP,” or ”Ingress Protection” rating. This rating consists of two digits:.

Noise Cancellation vs Ambient Awareness.

Picking between noise cancellation and ambient awareness for your running headphones is like choosing your own adventure. If you're dodging chatty pedestrians in the urban jungle, ambient awareness—whether that be found in typical earbuds or open-ear style headphones—might be your best bet, keeping you alert to honks and “behind you” shouts. But if you’re hitting the serene trails, craving that deep focus, or you have really noisy coworkers or hate the sound of grunting gym bros, let noise cancellation be your peaceful respite, blocking out everything but the sound of your own steady rhythm and, perhaps, a suspenseful podcast.

Battery life is essential for running headphones, especially for long distances. Will these headphones endure the entirety of your week’s run plan without dying? I’m terrible at remembering to charge my stuff, so this is crucial for folks like me.

It has been revealed that connectivity is also important. Most running headphones use Bluetooth, and the range can vary. Ideally, you want a stable connection that won't drop out when your phone is a few steps away. Typical Bluetooth range is around 30 feet, but interference can reduce this. Some newer headphones offer improved Bluetooth versions for greater range and stability.

Industry observers note that headphones, like other gadgets, have firmware that controls their functions and features. Manufacturers often release updates to improve performance, add fresh features, or fix complications with firmware, which can have bugs or limitations like any software. These updates are crucial for maintaining optimal functionality and ensuring compatibility with the latest devices and technologies.

Sources indicate that many of today's best headphones and earbuds have companion apps that allow users to manage and upgrade the firmware. Additionally, these updates may introduce fresh features (e.g., enhanced noise cancellation, improved call quality, and more customization options), all of which are managed through the partner app. Keeping the firmware up to date via the app ensures that the headphones perform optimally and offer the latest features.

Industry observers note that when it comes to running headphones, durability is honestly everything, because, who wants to buy a new pair every few months? Trust us, our team put these headphones through the wringer, testing them for weeks, sometimes even months and years (yep, we’re that dedicated) to find the ones that can actually keep up with your miles. We sweated on them, dropped them, stuffed them in gym bags, and even braved a few surprise rain showers—just to make sure they’re as tough as your training routine. So, when we say these are the best running headphones for durability, you know we mean it.

To pinpoint the best running headphones, our team put each pair through thorough, real-world testing for weeks—and sometimes even months. (And not for anything, I’ve had a pair of the original Beats Pro for five years, and they’re still rocking.) We had all kinds of runners try them out, from marathoners to casual joggers, to make sure our results would work for everyone. This way, we got feedback on comfort, fit, and performance for every running style and distance.

Our tests weren’t just in one spot; we put these headphones through all sorts of situations to see how tough and functional they really are. This meant running in different weather, from sunshine to sudden downpours, and at various elevations to check their performance under varying physical stresses. We also tested them in places with different noise levels—from quiet trails where you don’t need to hear much around you, to busy city streets where safety and clear sound are super key.

Through this rigorous evaluation, we were able to pinpoint headphones that could withstand sweat, accidental drops, and general wear and tear associated with regular running. We paid close attention to factors like secure fit, battery life, sound quality, and the effectiveness of features like noise cancellation and ambient awareness in real-world scenarios.

How do you listen to music and run phone-free?

The latter has more features if you’re a multi-sport, stats-junkie, but the price is significantly higher. The watches allow you to sync with music providers, such as Spotify. Most earbuds, with the exception of Apple Airpods, are Garmin compatible.

Industry observers note that for a deep clean, fill a glass with a drop of dish soap in half a cup of warm water. Remove the foam or silicone tips from the earbuds, and let them soak in the soap mixture for 30 minutes. Use a cotton swab or Q-Tip to remove excess particles. Allow the tips to air dry before screwing them back on. Use a clean old toothbrush to gently scrub the actual earbuds, mesh cover pointed down.

Whey protein powder is a popular supplement because it’s a simple and effective way to increase daily protein intake.

Whey is a complete protein that contains all nine essential amino acids our bodies need to build muscle. Whey protein also supplies the body with branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), like leucine, which help promote muscle growth (1).

We consulted Pete Nastasi, a certified nutrition coach (C.N.C.), to help us find the best whey protein powders on the market.

Here, we break down the different types of whey protein powders available (concentrate, isolate, and hydrolysate), which types will work best for you, and what nutrition information to look for. Plus, we’ve tested over 50 protein powders to help us create the list of our top picks.

In a recent development, medical disclaimer: This article is intended for educational and informational purposes only. It is not intended as a substitute for medical advice. For health advice, contact a licensed healthcare provider.

We chose products for our list of the best whey protein powders based on a number of factors reflected in our whey protein powder scoring methodology. These include:.

We also receive input from our panel of expert contributors, which includes registered dietitians and highly credentialed experts in sports nutrition and exercise science.

No sugar, all protein—that’s what Transparent Labs set out to accomplish with its grass-fed whey protein isolate. This whey protein undergoes filtration (2), taking out the excess sugar, fat, carbs, and lactose so you’re giving your body the pure protein it needs to rebuild. Whey isolate has the highest protein concentration of the different types of protein powders, and this protein is a good option if you’re trying to reduce your carb and fat intake.

Transparent Labs’ Whey Protein Isolate packs 28 grams of protein into each serving—one of the highest on our list. We also like the flavor variety, including unique flavors like Cinnamon French Toast. Bonus: This protein isn’t too sweet, so you can mix it with fruit juice or add it to a fruit smoothie without feeling like you’re drinking a shake made with Fun Dip.

Sports Research Whey Protein is formulated with 6.9 grams of BCAAs, including 1,000 milligrams of L-leucine. Studies show leucine may help reduce delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS). Depending on flavor, this Informed Sport Certified protein powder is sweetened with stevia or sucralose, so those sensitive to these ingredients may need to steer clear.

Rachel Pasche states she has a protein shake for dessert some nights using the Dutch Chocolate flavor. “It might be too sweet for some people, but I honestly love the taste so much,” she says. “It’s my favorite flavor of protein powder I’ve ever tried.” She says the powder mixes well with water alone, with both a handheld mixer and in a shaker cup, noting there is some foam at the top that doesn’t last long and no clumping.

Additionally, Pasche says she sometimes feels bloated after whey protein shakes, but after six months of using Sports Research Whey, she has not experienced any bloat.

Why is grass-fed whey protein better? Studies show that dairy sourced from grass-fed cows has a higher concentration of whey proteins and amino acids (3), which may further support muscular training adaptations.

According to recent reports, this Nutricost protein powder is non-GMO, gluten-free, and third-party tested. Whey protein concentrate, like this one, is often made with sunflower lecithin, an ingredient to help promote mixability. Testers also enjoy the taste and say this protein powder mixes well. “The taste was nostalgic; I’d liken it to Nesquik,” claims tester Grant Smith. “And the mixability was on par with some of the better proteins I’ve had previously.” Smith was pleasantly surprised by the mixability of Nutricost Whey Protein, noting he didn’t find any small chunks of undissolved protein floating in his shake when mixed with milk.

Industry observers note that after drinking most of his shake, Smith let a bit of the mixture sit for almost 10 minutes after initially mixing to test for separation. He noticed some slight separation between the protein and skim milk he mixed it with, but says it wasn’t enough to make the drink any less appealing.

Industry observers note that the protein in Legion Athletics is certified to contain no banned substances by Labdoor, the gold standard of third-party lab testing. This helps ensure the protein isolate is in its purest, most nutritionally dense form without any interference from pesticides and growth hormones.

In a recent development, additionally, Legion Athletics whey is filtered to remove extra carbs and fat, so you’re only getting the good stuff with every serving. The removal of these elements is geared toward bloat-free digestion.

Testers say it also tastes great, giving especially high marks to the French Vanilla flavor. “I really like the flavor of this one. It tastes like a vanilla creamer!” says Kayla Godfrey. “This is delicious. Great vanilla taste,” says Carlo Barajas.

Recent findings suggest that you’ve probably seen that one of the biggest general complaints about protein powder is it can taste “chalky” and leave you with an off-putting aftertaste. Our testing team tried Gainful’s Caffe Mocha flavor, and liked the subtle, not-too-sweet flavor profile. “This reminds me of an at-home cappuccino mix,” states Barry Bridges. “The coffee flavor is very light—I’d say it’s more of a chocolate flavor,” adds Rachael Harris.

If you’re not a fan of coffee flavors, Gainful offers nine total flavors in individual-use packets, so you can pick and choose what you’re craving each day. Nastasi, who has tried many different Gainful Protein Powder flavors, says the Chocolate Peanut Butter, Caffe Mocha, and Sea Salt Caramel are his favorites.

Whey protein is a concentrated protein source derived from cow’s milk, which contains two major proteins called casein and whey (4). Whey accounts for 20 percent of milk protein, and is considered a high-quality protein source. Cow’s milk protein is considered a complete protein because it contains all nine essential amino acids required by the body (5).

Recent findings suggest that beyond basic nutrition, whey protein (6) may offer specific health benefits, such as enhanced immune function (7) and cardiometabolic health (8). Usually, whey is sold in powder form, which can be blended with water or other liquids or added to soft foods. Also, people use whey protein powder in cooking, which adds nutritional value to baked goods. Food manufacturers use whey formulations rather than cream, butter, or egg ingredients to make high-protein, low-fat products.

When you browse online or at your local nutrition shop for whey protein products, you’ll probably notice different forms of whey. The main difference in the types of whey protein is how they’re processed. The three most common forms of whey protein are concentrate, isolate, and hydrolysate (hydrolyzed whey).

Whey protein concentrate (WPC) is the least processed form of whey, so it contains the highest levels of lactose (milk sugar), fat, carbohydrates, and nutrients. Food manufacturers use WPC (9) to replace fresh dairy and eggs in products like sauces, soups, and baked goods because it adds flavor, color, and texture and extends shelf-life (10). However, it has the lowest protein content out of the three—typically 70 to 80 percent.

It has been revealed that whey protein isolate (WPI) is made when whey is filtered and processed. It contains the most protein, 90 percent or more, and less lactose. Because of its higher protein content, sports nutrition companies often prefer WPI for use in supplements, protein bars, and other protein products (11). However, it lacks some of the beneficial nutrients found in the concentrated form (12).

In a recent development, whey protein hydrolysate (WPH), also known as hydrolyzed whey, is produced by a process called partial hydrolysis, which breaks down whey protein for easier absorption (13). WPH is digested faster than WPC or WPI (14), so it causes a 28 to 43 percent increase in blood sugar levels (15). Diabetics don’t have to worry about this, though. Protein digestion is slow. In fact, recent research suggests that whey protein improves glycemic (blood sugar) control (16).

Industry observers note that the real benefit of a whey protein powder is that it’s an incredibly convenient and high-quality source of dietary protein. However, if you consume enough dietary protein through meat, dairy, legumes, and other foods, then you don’t need a protein powder to achieve your health and fitness goals. However, if you’re having trouble consuming enough protein through your diet alone, then adding a protein powder to your daily routine can have some real benefits.

It has been revealed that whey protein is rich in essential amino acids, including BCAAs, which can be beneficial for supporting muscle integrity and growth with training (17). Adding a protein powder for muscle gain to your daily diet can be a great way to help maximize your dietary protein intake and stimulate muscle growth.

It has been revealed that when you’re in a caloric deficit with the goal of losing weight, you want to ensure that the weight you’re losing is primarily fat and not muscle. Eating a diet rich in protein helps preserve the lean muscle mass you’ve worked hard to achieve and enables your body to prioritize burning fat for energy.

It has been revealed that consuming whey protein has a satiating effect, meaning that it helps you feel full for a longer period of time. High protein diets help with weight loss by regulating your hunger levels and therefore reducing the amount of total calories you consume throughout the day.

In a recent development, in order to properly use a whey protein powder, you should first determine how much protein you should be eating on a daily basis. The amount of protein you consume is dependent on your fitness goals and current body weight, activity level, and physique. A simple way to calculate your daily protein intake is by multiplying your body weight by 0.8. The resulting number is how many grams of protein you should consume each day. This should provide most active individuals with sufficient protein intake. Remember that whey protein powder is a supplement and shouldn’t be your main source of dietary protein.

It has been revealed that as far as how to consume this protein powder, you should follow the instructions on the supplement label. This usually entails mixing one scoop of protein powder with 10 to 12 ounces of your favorite beverage. It can also be mixed in a smoothie or foods like oatmeal and pancake batter. Whey protein powder can be consumed at any time of the day, but it’s usually utilized as a post-workout supplement to begin repairing muscle tissue.

When used in moderation, protein powder is free of side effects and generally considered safe for healthy adults. However, consuming large amounts of protein powder can lead to digestive issues, dehydration, and (potentially) nutrient deficiencies. It’s important to use whey protein powder as part of a balanced diet and not as your main source of dietary protein. If you experience any unusual symptoms after using protein powder, stop use immediately and consult a healthcare professional.

A whey protein powder will benefit anyone who is looking to increase their daily protein consumption and has trouble doing so through their diet alone. This is especially relevant for very active individuals, such as athletes, bodybuilders, and fitness enthusiasts who have increased protein demands due to their workouts and training.

Recent findings suggest that another segment of the population that may benefit from using a whey protein powder is older adults. As we age, our bodies become less efficient at absorbing protein from food (18). Using protein supplements can be an easy way for older adults to meet their daily protein needs and support muscle health.

When picking a whey protein product, there are a few factors to consider, including the type of protein, taste, nutrition, additives/allergies, and price.

Check the ingredients list to see what type of whey the protein powder contains. Some brands will use a blend of whey forms.

Whey proteins come in a wide variety of flavors. You’ll find options from unflavored to vanilla, chocolate orange, and summer berries, to name a few. Taste is important because you want a protein supplement you’ll enjoy. When just starting to supplement your protein intake, try a small container or buy samples of flavors you might enjoy and get creative with your add-ins. You can try fruits, flavored milks, or juices to create new flavors that fit your taste preference.

Industry observers note that check the whey protein label for the amount of protein per serving, and factor it into your daily protein intake. Most protein powders have around 25 grams per serving, which is an ideal dosage to maximize muscle protein synthesis (19). Also look for calories, fats, carbs, fiber, vitamins, and minerals and even amino acid profiles. Make sure that the supplement you choose gives you the maximum benefit without unnecessary add-ins.

Read the ingredients section, too. Look for additives or allergens that you want or need to avoid. For example, labels warn you if the whey powder contains soy or was processed in a facility with nuts.

According to recent reports, the protein powders on our list give you a good idea of the price range for whey supplements. Our top picks vary from $1.16 to $3.41 per serving or $34 to $95 per container, so there’s an option for most budgets.

Industry observers note that it depends on your body’s unique needs and health and fitness goals. You should include protein with meals or snacks every three to five hours (20), but no one should rely solely on protein powder because that would eliminate other nutritious whole foods from the diet.One whey protein drink per day is reasonable. Check with your doctor if you want to use whey protein to replace more than one meal.

Yes, whey protein powder is generally considered safe for healthy individuals when used in moderation. If you have any pre-existing medical conditions or have a severe lactose intolerance, consult with a healthcare professional before adding a whey protein powder to your diet.

According to recent reports, there really is no “best time” to take a whey protein powder supplement. Instead, your timing depends on your individual goals and lifestyle. Some people enjoy a protein shake in the morning as a quick and easy breakfast option they can have on the go, while others prefer to consume it immediately after a workout to support muscle growth and recovery.Just remember that whey protein powder should be used as a supplement to a well-balanced diet, and should not be used as a replacement for whole nutrient-dense foods. The timing of when you consume the whey protein is less important than your overall protein intake throughout the day.

According to recent reports, from keeping you satiated to helping you improve your performance in the gym, whey protein powder can certainly help you lose weight. Research has even shown that whey protein may reduce abdominal fat when combined with weight training (21).

Recent findings suggest that if overused, whey protein can cause side effects (22), including kidney or liver damage, aggression, acne, and a disruption in gut bacteria. Since most people don’t consume more than one serving of whey protein per day, overconsumption is rare and takes time to develop. If you would like to add an extra layer of protection for your gut bacteria, you can even take a high-quality prebiotic or ensure you consume a variety of fruits and vegetables on a regular basis.

  • In a recent development, since 1985, this unique annual race has been taking place on the unforgiving flanks of the High Tatras mountains in Slovakia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that running up a rocky and technical trail more than a mile above sea level is tricky enough. Imagine doing it with a keg of beer strapped to your back—because this is exactly what competitors in the Sherpa Rallye, held on October 24, had to contend with.

Recent findings suggest that male entrants in the race shoulder a traditional wooden carrying frame, which resembles a sled but is loaded high with a 30-liter (about 8 gallons) keg of beer, plus other supplies (including large bottles of water) that add up to more than 130 pounds (60 kg). Women commonly carry cases of beer and materials that make their load weigh about 44 pounds (20 kg).

In a recent development, since 1985, this unique annual race has been taking place on the unforgiving flanks of the High Tatras mountains in Slovakia. It starts just above the town of Starý Smokovec and finishes at Zbojnícka chata, a mountain refuge perched like an alpine eyrie 3.5 miles up the steep and rough track.

Recent findings suggest that the High Tatras are home to Europe’s last remaining group of old-school mountain porters, many of whom take part in the race, which was started by a porter named Viktor Beránek to help bring workers together. They are locally and colloquially known as horský šerpa (mountain sherpas)—although they have no connection to the Sherpas of the Tibetan Himalaya, a distinct ethnic group, and are more correctly called horský nosi (mountain carriers).

In a recent development, however you refer to them, each season they manually transport heavy supplies to the mountain huts, refuges, and chalets that hikers use for shelter while trekking the local trails. And herein lies the rub, because once the Sherpa Rallye runners reach Zbojnícka chata, they don’t even get to celebrate by supping the goods they have just transported up to the hut—it goes in the stores for use over winter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article. Why Trust Us?

After months of long runs and tough workouts, you’ve finally crossed the finish line of your goal race. Now, it’s time to recover—and figure out what’s next.

Sources indicate that while you can scale back your running in the offseason, it’s worth making room for strength training. Even a short time in the weight room can help you build a stronger foundation for your next training block.

The good news? You don’t need to spend all your newfound free time in the gym to make progress. By hitting the following minimum amount of strength work each week, you set yourself up to handle more mileage and run more efficiently when it’s time to chase a new goal.

In the first two weeks after your race, you should focus mainly on rest and getting back into easy jogging. After that, aim to add at least two strength sessions per week to your routine, exercise physiologist Heather Milton, C.S.C.S., previously told Runner’s World. Milton indicates these offseason strength sessions should focus on heavier weights (just make sure you work up in weight!) and a low-to-moderate number of reps.

During these heavy lifting workouts, athletes should aim to complete four to six sets of one to five reps of each exercise, pausing for two to four minutes in between each set, strength coach and physical therapist Lisbeth Hoyt, D.P.T., C.S.C.S., previously told Runner’s World.

Industry observers note that while running is your main focus during marathon training (or any race distance, for that matter), strength sessions often help you maintain the strength you already have, Milton explains. But between training blocks, you can put more emphasis on building strength.

“Plus, when you start training for your next marathon, you’ll be in a stronger position to increase your running volume again because you’ve strengthened all of the areas of your body that were impacted by your previous race, which can help prevent injuries,” Milton adds.

You might associate heavy lifting with short sprinters or football players—athletes who focus on quick, explosive movement, rather than steady endurance. But building stronger muscles through heavy lifting supports long-distance running, too.

For starters, lifting heavier weights helps you build muscular strength, which translates to improved running economy, Newly introduced York City-based strength and run coach Yusuf Jeffers previously told Runner’s World. Meaning, heavy lifting can help you use less energy to run at a given pace.

Research backs this up. A review published in Sports Medicine in 2023 examined several types of strength training in middle- and long-distance runners, including lifting heavy, submaximal lifting, isometric exercises, and plyometrics. The researchers found that lifting high loads—at least 80 percent of a person’s one-rep max—had the greatest effect on improving running economy at faster speeds. (Plyometrics worked particularly well for improving economy at slower speeds.).

The benefits extend beyond your muscles, too. Hoyt explains that strength training can support connective tissues and bone health.

It’s key to remember lifting “heavy” looks different for everyone. If you’re latest to strength training or you’re unfamiliar with a particular movement, start by learning proper form and gradually work up in weight, Hoyt states.

Hoyt suggests focusing on movements such as squats, deadlifts, lunges, and rows, encouraging athletes to move slowly and with control.

I Put the “No Headphones on the Bike” Rule to the Test and Found a Better Way to Listen

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Sources indicate that many of us have been through a bad experience or two thanks to trail people listening to music on a ride.
  • However, not all who listen to music on the trail are this oblivious.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. How we test gear.

Sources indicate that many of us have been through a bad experience or two thanks to trail people listening to music on a ride. Sometimes it’s not even a dangerous situation—I can think of more than a few situations where I spooked a fellow rider listening to music while they pedal along in their own little bubble. It’s not just with cyclists. I’ve rolled up on cyclists, hikers, and trail runners alike who are surprised by my presence—even after ringing my bell, calling on your left numerous times, and letting my freehub ratchet away to try and get their attention.

However, not all who listen to music on the trail are this oblivious. I’ve been riding for close to two decades and I’ve spent a lot of time in the saddle both listening to music and not. There are times popping in a headphone makes sense and times when it isn’t the right call. But there is a right and wrong way to do it, even on those rides I consider to be the right times.

This year I’ve tried out different types of headphones to see what works, what doesn’t, and ways to avoid letting a little music ruin someone else’s ride.

Last year Matt Phillips, our Senior Test Editor at Bicycling, wrote a story about his almost literal run-in with another cyclist on the trail. “Bright red Beats earbuds. Music blasting so loud I could hear the song,” said Phillips about the rider who almost collided with him head-on. Phillips goes on to point out that riding with headphones can put people in a bubble. Riding in a way that can cause safety problems on the trail for yourself and other users is irresponsible, but there’s a better way to listen to music and navigate these shared spaces.

Sources indicate that I’ve been using traditional headphones for years—typically riding with only one headphone in while I ride. This year I’ve tried a few different bone-conducting headphones and I thought they were a huge step in the right direction. They give listeners a better ability to be aware of their surroundings while listening to music compared to traditional earbuds. And save those bulky headphones, like the Bose QuietComfort, for your trainer rides.

I’ve been using the Shokz Open Run 2 headphones for about six months now and I love them for riding outside. The headphones allow me to hear my surroundings and still get a musical boost when I need it. While I’ve been using these headphones, I typically only wear one earbud and let the other side just hang around my neck.

The Open Run headphones are not individual earbuds like common AirPods—the Open Run 2 has a band that connects the left and right, so if you want to only have one ear listening, the other side just hangs out by your neck. Bone-conducting headphones were a step in the right direction to be more aware while jamming out on the bike, but recently I’ve gotten to try a different style of headphones that may have solved this problem once and for all.

Of all the headphones I’ve tried for riding outside, my two current top choices go to the Bose Sport Open Earbuds and the Shokz Open Dots 2. Both of these headphones use what’s called air conduction technology. They essentially sit just outside your ear and direct the sound into your ear through the air. This style of headphone gives the situational awareness of bone conduction headphones, but without pressing on your outer ear to pump sound through.

Recent findings suggest that my initial concern was how secure can this style of headphone really be? When I first clipped them on my ears, I didn’t think they would stay on during a gravel ride, let alone bouncing around on chunky singletrack.

After testing both of them in situations where I was trying to bounce or knock them out I was pleasantly surprised—I still have two complete pairs of earbuds. Mountain biking with a half-shell and full-face helmet, fast road descents, bouncing off trees on the gravel bike, and even downhill trail runs on technical trails couldn’t bounce these out of my ears. These headphones make it easy to have one headphone in and maintain a healthy awareness of other trail users.

Recent findings suggest that if I had to pick between the Bose Sport Open Earbuds and the Shokz Open Dots 2 I would choose the Bose Sport Open Earbuds. On the Bose, the button to control the headphones was easy to use even with gloves on and when the headphones shifted a little on my ear the sound quality remained high. The Shokz Open Dots are a good pair of headphones, but the controls on the Shokz Open Dots 2 are a bit harder to use while wearing gloves. I thought the sound quality was a notch better in the Bose Open Earbuds compared to the Shokz Open Dots too. If you’re someone who likes to listen to music while you’re in the saddle, then check out these Bose Sport Open Earbuds and the Shokz Open Dots 2.

‘Just a Guy With a Boat on His Head’: He’s Running 52 Marathons in 52 Weeks—While Carrying a Canoe Every Step

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Getting to the Philadelphia Marathon on November 22 proved an endurance event of its own for Travis Meier.
  • And yes, the canoe made it through the entire race without ever touching water.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Coming from Minnesota, I can't just throw a boat in an overhead compartment," Meier told Runner's World.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Getting to the Philadelphia Marathon on November 22 proved an endurance event of its own for Travis Meier. The 38-year-old Minneapolis resident flew into Hartford, Connecticut, drove three hours into the Adirondack Mountains to pick up a canoe, then spent another five hours behind the wheel getting to Philadelphia. This was all before tackling Sunday’s 26.2 miles with the boat balanced over his head.

And yes, the canoe made it through the entire race without ever touching water.

Recent findings suggest that “Coming from Minnesota, I can't just throw a boat in an overhead compartment," Meier told Runner's World. "It was a logistical nightmare: where to keep it, where to sneak it into the race, and how people would react to it.".

Despite the travel headaches, Meier came away from Philadelphia with his second personal record in as many weeks. It was another step in his latest undertaking: 52 marathons in 52 weeks, each while carrying a canoe, to raise awareness about protecting the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness in northern Minnesota.

Recent findings suggest that meier, who manages a distillery when he isn't hauling boats around, wasn't exactly a seasoned runner when all this started. His introduction to the sport came through the Red Bull Urban Portage, an event that involved carrying a boat through downtown Minneapolis before paddling along the Mississippi River.

It has been revealed that “I was really bad at paddling, but I could outrun people,” he recalled. Before the event, he bought a Northstar ADK canoe off Craigslist with every intention of selling it once the race was over. Instead, it found a home on his garage wall and managed to stick around for another year. Eventually, he started entering more races with it.

It has been revealed that that eventually brought him to Minnesota's Ely Marathon in 2023, where he completed his first-ever 26.2-mile race while carrying a canoe. Since then, he's run only one conventional marathon without a boat, and what started solely as a personal experiment gradually became an opportunity to draw attention to a place he'd loved for years.

The Boundary Waters, a wilderness area known for its lakes, forests, and extensive canoe routes, has been at the center of a contentious debate over proposed mining operations. Federal protections restricting mining in the surrounding watershed were rolled back earlier this year, a development that particularly frustrated Meier.

According to recent reports, "I've been to many remote places on this earth, and very few have its caliber of perfect,” he said. “So why would someone want to mess it up?".

Meier had been toying with the idea of running 52 marathons in 52 weeks ever since reading about Dane Rauschenberg, who accomplished the feat in 2006. With the ongoing fight over protections for the Boundary Waters, he had his reason to give it a shot, bringing his canoe as a form of protest to May’s Taco Bell 50K. It got people asking questions, which was exactly what he wanted, and gave him encouragement to keep showing up at races with a boat on his head.

Of course, carrying a canoe for more than four hours at a time comes with some challenges, particularly when Mother Nature gets involved.

During the Mankato Marathon in Minnesota, Meier battled 30mph winds along a ridge beside a cornfield. Mile 14 alone took him nearly 22 minutes, as his canoe repeatedly caught the wind and spun him around like a kite.

At one point, Meier turned to a few supporters witnessing him get thrown around and asked, “When's the point of insanity?” He sent them ahead to see if the wind conditions were better ahead in the valley. Luckily, the gusts let up enough, sparing him a repeat trip through that nightmare.

The spectators in Philadelphia offered a different kind of entertainment, with plenty to say about the guy running a marathon with a canoe on his head.

Around mile three, Meier encountered a young girl who appeared scared by the enormous object approaching her. He knelt down, giving her enough confidence to return his high-five.

"Grandmas confess their love to me, and I don't know why," he remarked of his interactions with spectators, adding that Philadelphia set a record for the number of phallic jokes he heard along the course.

The jokes are part of the experience, and the attention is ultimately what he's hoping for. Meier stated fellow runners often approach him after a race to discuss the Boundary Waters and the larger issue of protecting public lands. He's also seen Instagram comments from people who knew little about the area before coming across his videos.

"They may not know anything, but they've at least gotten a 10,000-foot view of the BWCA," he said.

Industry observers note that the running community has helped make the challenge possible, with sponsors pitching in for race entries and shoes while Meier covers the remaining expenses. He's even promised to refund their donations if he doesn't complete the challenge.

"My integrity is everything,” he mentioned, “even though I'm not a organization, just a guy with a boat on his head.”.

His biggest sacrifice so far has been giving up so much of his free time. Between a full-time job, travel, recovery, and the weekly races, there’s no room for a vacation abroad. He has considered tackling back-to-back marathons to create some breathing room. His body hasn't agreed to the arrangement.

Recent findings suggest that as for what would make all 52 races worthwhile, Meier has a specific outcome in mind: permanent legislation protecting the Boundary Waters. Here’s the good news: proposals exist in both the House of Representatives and Senate. Even so, he knows that may be a tall order. But his presence—and effort—are creating awareness.

"If it doesn't happen, which it likely won't, at least the effort started conversations about our public lands," he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When someone states they want to lose weight, what they really mean is they want to shed excess body fat. However, without a well-designed plan in place, a calorie deficit leads you to lose both fat and valuable muscle tissue. To minimize muscle loss, it’s crucial to incorporate resistance training, quality sleep, and a high-protein diet into your regular routine.

Protein plays a multifaceted role in weight management, influencing factors like hunger levels, metabolism, and muscle preservation. While heavy resistance training provides the necessary stimulus, signaling to the body that existing muscle should be retained, a high-protein diet ensures the body has an ample supply of amino acids. This prevents your body from metabolizing muscle tissue for energy.

The best protein powders provide a convenient and lean source of the muscle-building macronutrient, helping you hit your daily protein goals while also maintaining a calorie deficit. We tested more than 100 protein powders and selected nine products we think are best for weight loss.

This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any upcoming supplement or exercise regimen.

We chose these products based on a number of factors, including:.

I chose Transparent Labs as the best protein powder for weight loss because it has a very high ratio of protein to the total number of calories: 28 grams to 130 calories. This helps you maximize protein consumption during a caloric deficit, which helps prevent you from losing muscle while you’re losing weight. It’s also third-party tested, Informed Choice certified, and completely artificial ingredient-free. And it comes in 15 flavor options.

It has been revealed that I’ve tried a number of different flavors from Transparent Labs and Chocolate Peanut Butter is by far my favorite, followed closely by Mocha. I found they mixed easily in both a blender and a conventional shaker bottle. Whenever I’m trying to cut weight, I find this delicious protein powder helps curb my sweet tooth and tide me over between meals.

While I didn’t personally experience this, some customer reviews mention it can be challenging to get in contact with Transparent Labs’ customer service team.

In a recent development, jacked Factory Authentic Iso has 25 grams of protein per serving, 2 grams of carbohydrates, and just 0.5 grams of fat, which is the least amount of fat of any powder on our list. If you’re looking to lose weight, this macronutrient profile will help keep you on the right track. However, something to keep in mind: This protein powder is sweetened with sucralose, which is an artificial sweetener—studies link these sweeteners to increased cancer risk. Additionally, unlike most brands on our list, Jacked Factory doesn’t do third-party testing on its products. This means there isn’t a guarantee the ingredients are pure and match the ingredient label.

Kessler tried Jacked Factory Authentic Iso and was impressed. “This is the only protein powder I’ve tried that didn’t settle at all,” he states. “I found it a bit too sweet, but if you’re looking for a powder that tastes like dessert, you should opt for this one.”.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for one of the best vegan protein powders that also works with a weight loss diet, Ka’Chava is a great choice. This vegan protein powder is marketed as a “whole-body meal,” which means it’s designed as a meal replacement rather than an addition to a meal or snack, like the other protein powders on our list. That’s why the calorie, carbohydrate, and fat counts (240, 25 grams, and 7 grams, respectively), are higher. The carb count is high for those on a low-carb diet, so that’s something to look out for. However, it packs in 25 grams of plant protein, derived from a combination of peas, brown rice, and quinoa, which will help preserve muscle while on a weight loss diet.

Industry observers note that tester Zoe Ettinger, a C.N.C.-in-training, uses this protein powder often. “I’m a major fan of Ka’Chava. It tastes delicious mixed in a smoothie with some frozen blueberries,” she claims. “I also like that it also has adaptogens, probiotics, greens, and probiotics. I notice a difference in how good I feel when I take Ka’Chava regularly,” she says.

It has been revealed that one thing to note about Ka’Chava is that it is the most expensive option on our list at $79.99 for a 15-serving bag. While the price reflects the fact that this protein powder is intended as a meal replacement, it’s still a massive investment.

In a recent development, I chose Nutricost as the best protein powder for weight loss available on Amazon because its calorie and macronutrient profile is ideal for shedding pounds. Nutricost has a high protein content per serving, which is important for weight loss as protein can help enhance satiety and preserve muscle mass while in a deficit. With minimal fat and carbohydrates, this protein ensures you get the maximum protein intake without the added calories, making it an ideal choice for those looking to lose weight efficiently.

The taste and mixability of this protein are also top-notch. I tested the Vanilla flavor; it blended excellently in both milk and water and had an authentic vanilla taste profile. Despite using artificial sweeteners, which often make products sickly sweet, I found the sweetness level to be on point. However, if you’re trying to avoid artificial sweeteners, choose Promix or Transparent Labs, which use natural sweeteners.

Industry observers note that huel is our favorite meal replacement for weight loss because it has a great protein-to-carb ratio. Huel has 40 grams of protein per serving, the most of any protein powder on our list, and 24 grams of carbs. While this might be more carbs than ideal for those on a keto diet, it’s a solid portion for most. Carbs are an essential nutrient and according to experts, you can consume 100 to 150 grams a day and still lose weight.

Recent findings suggest that kessler tried Huel in Chocolate and Vanilla. “The Chocolate flavor was great, probably because it uses real cocoa powder, which gave it an authentic chocolate flavor,” he claims. “The Vanilla wasn’t as good—it didn’t really taste like vanilla and had an artificial aftertaste.” He notes that it doesn’t mix very well, but says it made him feel great. “Other similar products, like Transparent Labs Mass Gainer, give me an upset stomach. It has been revealed that promix is our favorite clean protein powder because it’s third-party tested and results are easily viewable on Promix’s website. This protein powder, like others on our list, has a solid protein-to-carb ratio for weight loss (25 grams to 7 grams, respectively). A 2020 study found consuming a higher portion of protein versus carbs helped participants lose weight and prevented them from gaining the weight back.

According to recent reports, I tried the Vanilla flavor of this protein powder. I enjoyed it for the most part, but it wasn’t quite sweet enough for my taste. And I wish it mixed a little better—there were some clumps after mixing.

One thing to note about Promix is that while it has been third-party tested, it hasn’t been third-party tested for sport specifically. This means it hasn’t been tested for substances banned in athletic competitions. So if you’re an athlete planning to compete, opt for a powder that’s Informed Sport Certified or NSF Certified for Sport.

Sources indicate that one of my favorite casein protein powders is Casein+ from Legion Athletics. I chose Casein+ because it’s all-natural, meaning it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors, and it’s third-party tested by Labdoor for purity and potency. This product provides 25 grams of protein per serving and only contains 110 calories, regardless of the flavor you choose. This protein-to-calorie ratio is ideal for weight loss.

Industry observers note that along with whey, casein is a type of protein found in milk and is characterized by its slow digestion and absorption. This prolonged digestion makes it an ideal option for people looking to manage hunger levels and maintain a consistent supply of amino acids over an extended timeframe—such as during sleep or when going a long time between meals. By providing a steady stream of protein to the muscles, casein helps mitigate the risk of muscle breakdown that often accompanies calorie restriction. As a result, incorporating a casein protein powder into your diet can be a strategic move to help support your weight loss goals.

Recent findings suggest that tester Brandon Lunsford, C.P.T., tried the Dutch Chocolate flavor, saying it reminded him of a dark chocolate bar that isn’t too rich or too sweet. Naked Whey’s Unflavored protein stands out for its simplicity and purity; its single-ingredient formula consists of whey protein concentrate sourced for grass-fed cows. Industry observers note that from a nutritional standpoint, Sports Research stacks up well against many of its competitors. Whether from powder or whole food sources, protein aids weight loss mainly by:.

Protein powder can be an effective tool in helping you achieve your weight loss goals. Drinking a protein powder shake or smoothie provides a quick, easy way to consume high amounts of protein with a limited amount of calories, fat, and carbohydrates. One of the main benefits of protein powder is that it’s often extremely lean, with a very high ratio of protein to total number of calories. This makes protein powder an efficient way to hit your daily protein target while adhering to your calorie guidelines.

According to recent reports, choose a protein powder with a significant amount of protein, typically around 25 grams per serving. If you have weight loss goals, a whey, soy, or pea protein isolate is likely your best bet since they are ultra-filtered to remove excess carbohydrates and fats.

When you have weight loss goals, it’s best to choose a protein powder with a moderate calorie count per serving, e.g., 100 to 160 calories. You should also ensure the majority of those calories come from protein, as this will best support your weight loss progress. Remember, protein is four calories per gram, so you can expect a supplement that has 25 grams of protein to have around 110 to 120 calories if it’s extremely lean.

According to recent reports, it’s crucial to check the ingredients list of the supplement to ensure the product is free from added sugars or unnecessary fillers. Although these ingredients may contribute to the flavor, sweetness, and creaminess of the supplement, they often come with added calories. It’s generally best to select protein powders with minimal ingredients.

In a recent development, occasionally, protein powders contain ingredients such as creatine, probiotics, or branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). While these aren’t necessary, it’s key to assess whether these added ingredients align with your health and fitness goals, and whether it’s worth choosing a protein powder that offers these options.

It has been revealed that regardless of your goals, choose a protein powder with a flavor and consistency you enjoy. I know this seems obvious, but if you dislike the taste, then you’re far less likely to use the protein powder on a consistent basis, if at all.

Sources indicate that as a certified nutrition coach, I advise my clients to choose a protein powder that’s been third-party tested for quality, purity, and safety, especially when I’m working with athletes. This ensures your supplement is free from contaminants, including banned substances, and is deemed safe for consumption. Third-party testing also holds supplement companies accountable, providing assurance that the ingredients in the product align with the information provided on the supplement facts label.

Whenever you’re purchasing a dietary supplement, you should look for one that aligns with your specific health and fitness goals. With weight loss in mind, it’s typically recommended to avoid products with added sugars, or excessive amounts of carbohydrates and fats. Some consumers may also choose to avoid products with artificial additives, such as sweeteners, flavors, and colors, which are routinely found in protein powder supplements. If you’re looking for an all-natural protein powder with minimal ingredients, consider Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey or protein powders from Naked Nutrition.

According to recent reports, as a certified nutrition coach, I think it’s notable to emphasize that a protein powder isn’t a necessity for weight loss success. However, due to its convenience and effectiveness, it does offer some notable benefits when used as part of a holistic approach to weight loss that includes resistance training, quality sleep, and healthy lifestyle habits. Consuming a high-protein diet, especially during a weight-loss phase, helps manage hunger levels and improves muscle preservation. If a protein powder can help you hit your daily protein targets while still maintaining a calorie deficit, then I think it’s worth incorporating into your regular routine.

It has been revealed that protein shakes are an excellent way to help preserve lean muscle mass when pursuing your weight loss goals. If weight loss is your primary objective, I’d suggest opting for a whey protein isolate, such as Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey. This protein powder is incredibly lean, meaning the majority of calories come from protein alone. This can help you achieve your daily protein targets without over-consuming calories from the additional carbohydrates and fats commonly found in a whey protein concentrate.

It has been revealed that weight loss strategies vary from person to person, however, individuals with weight loss goals should aim for at least 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight. (This equates to approximately 0.5 to 0.7 grams of protein per pound of body weight.) This range should provide enough protein to support muscle mass while maintaining a calorie deficit, which is necessary for weight loss.

With protein powder for weight loss, certain protein sources are considered “leaner” than others. For example, whey protein isolates benefit from various kinds of processing and filtration that lower the fat and carbohydrates in the finished product. The main drawback with some plant-based proteins is that they can be naturally higher in carbs. Fortunately, high-quality plant protein powders could deliver comparable results to whey protein in terms of promoting lean body mass.Lean animal proteins include chicken breast, fish, and eggs. Even certain cuts of beef (sirloin) and pork (loin) are considered lean. Greek yogurt, tofu, beans, and lentils are among the non-animal sources of lean protein.

Industry observers note that when focusing on weight loss, it’s best to steer clear of calorie-rich beverages such as sugary sodas and sports drinks, fruit juices, and alcohol. Instead, choose options like water, seltzer, black coffee, and unsweetened tea, all of which are essentially calorie-free. Avoiding calorie-dense beverages allows you to allocate those calories to food instead, which should help improve your satiety or feelings of fullness after meals.

There’s no protein that targets belly fat loss specifically. However, prioritizing lean protein, such as a whey protein isolate, can be beneficial for your overall weight loss goals. Whey protein isolates are processed to minimize the carbohydrate and fat content, maximizing the protein-to-calorie ratio of the supplement. This makes them an efficient option to support your intake of dietary protein while maintaining a calorie deficit.
